top_10_batters.name: Rahul Tripathi
top_10_batters.why_target: High-tempo No. 3 with fearless intent against pace and spin. Directly replaces Sanju Samson at No. 3 with proven IPL pedigree (2,200+ career IPL runs).
top_10_batters.risks: Aggressive shot selection carries early dismissal risk against quality swing.

top_10_batters.name: Nitish Rana
top_10_batters.why_target: Elite middle-overs spin destructor. Smashes wrist-spin and SLA at 155+ SR, balancing RR middle order alongside Parag and Jurel.
top_10_batters.risks: Occasional vulnerability to back-of-a-length seam in powerplays.

top_10_batters.name: Nehal Wadhera
top_10_batters.why_target: High-ceiling young Indian left-handed finisher. Phenomenal composure in death chases (145+ SR), solves RR’s lower-order finishing void.
top_10_batters.risks: Still developing consistency against top-tier international mystery spin.

top_10_batters.name: Glenn Maxwell
top_10_batters.why_target: Generational T20 game-changer. Smashes both spin and pace at 180+ SR under pressure and provides 2–3 overs of off-spin on turning Jaipur pitches.
top_10_batters.risks: High-risk shot selection can lead to low-score strings; commands an overseas slot.

top_10_batters.name: Shimron Hetmyer
top_10_batters.why_target: Proven Rajasthan Royals match-winner. Re-acquiring him at a rational price after release provides instant death-overs boundary violence.
top_10_batters.risks: Utilizes 1 of RR’s 3 remaining overseas slots; price inflation in open bidding.

top_10_batters.name: M Shahrukh Khan
top_10_batters.why_target: High-impact domestic Indian boundary striker with 169+ pressure SR. Solves RR’s lower-order finishing without using an overseas slot.
top_10_batters.risks: Can be vulnerable to hard short-pitch bowling above shoulder height.

top_10_batters.name: Mahipal Lomror
top_10_batters.why_target: Ex-RR domestic talent with brutal spin power (162+ pressure SR) and useful slow left-arm bowling versatility.
top_10_batters.risks: Can be tied down by express pace targeted at the chest.

top_10_batters.name: Abishek Porel
top_10_batters.why_target: Dynamic Indian wicketkeeper providing essential glovework backup and aggressive top-order flexibility for Dhruv Jurel.
top_10_batters.risks: Relatively raw under extreme knockout match pressure.

top_10_batters.name: Rachin Ravindra
top_10_batters.why_target: World-class multi-phase accumulator and spin option. Provides top-order class and slow left-arm control at Sawai Mansingh Stadium.
top_10_batters.risks: Requires overseas slot; middle-overs boundary boundary rate needs elevation.

top_10_batters.name: Abhinav Manohar
top_10_batters.why_target: High-ceiling Indian domestic boundary striker (151.5 pressure SR). Fills middle-order depth and protects RR’s 3 remaining overseas slots.
top_10_batters.risks: Limited defensive gear if early wickets fall in powerplay.

top_10_bowlers.name: Matheesha Pathirana
top_10_bowlers.why_target: Generational death bowling phenom. 61 clutch wickets and 7.90 pressure economy. Pairs with Sandeep Sharma to form an impenetrable death-overs wall.
top_10_bowlers.risks: Workload management and shoulder/hamstring niggles; will command intense bidding war.

top_10_bowlers.name: Trent Boult
top_10_bowlers.why_target: Legendary Rajasthan Royals powerplay icon returning home. Immediate swing breakthroughs in overs 1–6, relieving pressure on Archer and Shami.
top_10_bowlers.risks: Age 37; diminished impact if pitch offers zero swing.

top_10_bowlers.name: Avesh Khan
top_10_bowlers.why_target: High-pace Indian death bowler with 57 clutch wickets. Protects RR’s overseas slots while delivering 145+ kph wide yorkers and hard bouncers.
top_10_bowlers.risks: Can be expensive when line errs onto pads in small grounds.

top_10_bowlers.name: Mustafizur Rahman
top_10_bowlers.why_target: World’s premier off-cutter and change-of-pace wizard. Exceptional 7.87 pressure economy on abrasive Sawai Mansingh Stadium pitches.
top_10_bowlers.risks: Vulnerable to straight-line power hitting if ball gets wet with dew.

top_10_bowlers.name: Wanindu Hasaranga
top_10_bowlers.why_target: Elite wicket-taking wrist-spinner (53 clutch wickets) paired with dynamic lower-order hitting power.
top_10_bowlers.risks: Can leak boundaries on flat batting tracks against elite spin hitters.

top_10_bowlers.name: Prasidh Krishna
top_10_bowlers.why_target: Proven 145+ kph Indian fast bowler who took 19 wickets for RR in IPL 2022. Hits the deck hard, generates steep bounce, and preserves overseas slots.
top_10_bowlers.risks: Past back stress fracture injury history requires ongoing physical load management.

top_10_bowlers.name: Deepak Chahar
top_10_bowlers.why_target: Premier Indian powerplay swing weapon and handy lower-order batsman. Provides domestic seam depth for RR.
top_10_bowlers.risks: Fitness fragility and limited effectiveness in death overs.

top_10_bowlers.name: Maheesh Theekshana
top_10_bowlers.why_target: Finger mystery spinner capable of bowling tight powerplay overs (7.94 pressure economy).
top_10_bowlers.risks: Limited boundary catching mobility; commands overseas slot.

top_10_bowlers.name: Tushar Deshpande
top_10_bowlers.why_target: Experienced domestic Indian seamer who strikes regularly in the middle and death overs (41 clutch wickets).
top_10_bowlers.risks: Prone to leaking boundary extras (10.22 pressure economy).

top_10_bowlers.name: Akash Deep
top_10_bowlers.why_target: High-intensity Indian pace bowler hitting a heavy length with test-match stamina. Protects domestic bowling reserves.
top_10_bowlers.risks: Can be targeted by ramp and scoop shots in death overs.
